Test Description: This testcase performs register-level read/write verification for the MIPI CSI2 RB register block (csi_reg block). The test validates two aspects: (1) Default/Reset Value Check — each readable register in the csi_reg block is read after reset and compared against its expected hardware default value; non-readable registers are skipped. (2) Write-Read-Back Check — a known data pattern is written to each writable register (skipping designated registers such as interrupt_raw and flush, as well as non-writable registers), then each register is read back and compared against an expected value that accounts for the register's read mask, write mask, and default value for non-writable bit positions. The test reports PASS if all registers match their expected values in both phases, and FAIL if any mismatch is detected in either phase.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1: Execute the default/reset value check phase. For each register in the csi_reg block, verify that the register is readable. If the register is not readable, skip it. If readable, read the register value and compare it against the expected default/reset value. Record any mismatch as a default-value failure.

Step 2: Execute the write-read-back verification phase. For each register in the csi_reg block, check whether the register is flagged to be skipped (interrupt_raw and flush are skipped in this phase). Also skip registers that are not writable. For all remaining writable registers, write a known data pattern to the register.

Step 3: After writing to all eligible registers, read back each written register. Skip registers that were not written, are not writable, or are not readable. For each read-back, compute the expected value by combining the written data (masked by the read and write masks) with the default value (for bit positions that are not writable but are readable). Compare the read-back value against this expected value. Record any mismatch as a write-read failure.

Step 4: Evaluate overall test result. If any default-value failures or write-read failures were recorded in the previous steps, report the test as FAIL. If no failures were recorded in either phase, report the test as PASS.
Impacted Registers: virtual_channel, line_info, fifo_threshold_val, lane_clk, mem, interrupt_raw, interrupt_mask, interrupt_enable, control_data, flush
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. Default Value Verification: For every readable register in the csi_reg block, the value read after reset must exactly match the expected default/reset value defined for that register. Any mismatch constitutes a failure.

2. Write-Read-Back Verification: For every writable and readable register (excluding skipped registers interrupt_raw and flush), the value read back after writing a known pattern must match the expected value. The expected value is computed by applying the write mask and read mask to the written data, combined with the default value for non-writable bit positions. Any mismatch constitutes a failure.

3. Overall Pass/Fail: The test passes (finish with success) only if zero default-value mismatches and zero write-read mismatches are recorded across all registers. Any non-zero failure count in either category results in test failure.
Remarks: The test covers 10 registers in the csi_reg block. Two registers (interrupt_raw and flush) are explicitly skipped during the write-read-back phase via a skip configuration. A soft reset check function exists in the test but is currently disabled (commented out) and is not executed during the test flow. Non-readable registers are automatically skipped during the default value check phase, and non-writable registers are automatically skipped during the write phase.
